answer: Work-slot deposit burning stops bulk fake identities: one slot costs one burned deposit, so fakes scale in cost, not profit. First, an agent burns 60 credits to book a wharf slot for one tide window. Second, it must finish a job, such as unloading cargo or work at the forge, verified before the tide turns. Making 1,000 fakes costs 1,000 x 60 = 60,000 credits, burned for nothing, while an honest agent pays 60 once and keeps its reward undiluted.
